readback.name: Poincare.ParabolicSpatialGraphPullback.exists_spatial_Graph_pullback
readback.mathematical_statement: E3 is EuclideanSpace R (Fin 3), the real three-dimensional Euclidean vector space in Type 0. Y alpha T V is the pinned normed graph space of total V-valued functions on R x E3 that are zero off the closed cylinder Icc 0 T times all of E3 and have bounded values and bounded scaled differences within that cylinder. Its norm is the value supremum plus the alpha-Hoelder seminorm over distinct ordered cylinder pairs, whose denominator is D(p,q)^alpha with D((t,x),(s,y)) = norm(x-y) + sqrt(abs(t-s)). The inserted zero in these suprema specifies the empty-set case. Y has no separate approximation, smoothness, or continuity condition across the endpoints of the zero extension. Graph alpha T has four Y fields: scalar u and ut, covector du, and continuous-bilinear-form-valued ddu, the latter represented as E3 ->L[R] E3 ->L[R] R. Its norm is the sum of the four Y norms. Its certificates state u(0,x) = 0 for every x; for every t in Icc 0 T and every x, the ordinary spatial Frechet derivative of z |-> u(t,z) is du(t,x), and that of z |-> du(t,z) is ddu(t,x); and the within-Icc 0 T time derivative of s |-> u(s,x) is ut(t,x). The first argument of ddu is the derivative direction and the second is the argument at which the resulting covector is evaluated. These time certificates do not assert an ordinary ambient time derivative at either endpoint or joint C3 regularity at initial time. For every total globally C-infinity F : E3 -> E3 with compact topological support and every real alpha satisfying 0 < alpha < 1, there exists a real C >= 0 such that for every T in the half-open interval Ioc 0 1, namely 0 < T <= 1, there exists a continuous real-linear map Q : Graph alpha T -> Graph alpha T with operator norm at most C. The bound C may depend on F and alpha, and is selected before T, so it is uniform for all 0 < T <= 1, all inputs G, and all evaluation points. For every G and every p = (t,x) in the entire ambient product R x E3, its four component identities are (Q G).u(t,x) = G.u(t,F(x)); (Q G).ut(t,x) = G.ut(t,F(x)); for every v, (Q G).du(t,x)(v) = G.du(t,F(x))(DF_x(v)); and for every v,w, (Q G).ddu(t,x)(v)(w) = G.ddu(t,F(x))(DF_x(v))(DF_x(w)) + G.du(t,F(x))(D2F_x(v)(w)). DF_x is fderiv R F x, while D2F_x is fderiv R (fderiv R F) x, with v in its derivative-direction slot and w in its application slot. The Hessian identity contains both the two-DF contraction and the additive second-derivative-of-F term. Time is unchanged, so ut has composition with F and no DF factor. The output belongs to the actual Graph structure and therefore carries its zero initial u trace and all three genuine derivative certificates, including the within-closed-time-interval certificate. The identities are not restricted to the cylinder, a chart overlap, or a cutoff support; off the cylinder all component equations are consistent with the Y zero extension because time is preserved. Compact topological support of F means the closure of the set where F is nonzero is compact, with no injectivity, invertibility, linearity, or affine hypothesis. C-infinity means ContDiff at the ENat top injected into WithTop ENat. Q is linear in G although F may be nonlinear. The u and ut formulas contain no scalar cutoff or source weight. In particular, wherever F(x) = 0 they evaluate the input at (t,0), so the statement does not assert compact spatial support for these output fields. T = 0, T < 0, and T > 1 are not covered by the operator-existence conclusion. No small-norm condition, inverse Q, atlas cocycle, tensor overlap compatibility, PDE identity, or ordinary joint C3 regularity at time zero is asserted. The declaration has no universe parameters.
